author: Bay State News
title: Northbridge man sentenced to probation after pleading guilty in brother's accidental shooting death
text:
Christopher Lacour, 34, was sentenced to five years of probation after pleading guilty to manslaughter in the shooting death of his brother, Johnathan S. “Jon” Lacour, 36, at their Northbridge family home, according to a June 10 hearing in Worcester Superior Court.
Lacour has maintained that the incident on May 21, 2025, was an accident. He initially pleaded not guilty but changed his plea during Wednesday’s court session. Judge Daniel M. Wrenn accepted the plea and imposed conditions including substance abuse evaluation and treatment if necessary, as well as a prohibition on possessing firearms.
Defense attorney Mark L. Monopoli recommended the agreed-upon five years of probation for Lacour. Assistant District Attorney Thomas Ayres had sought a sentence of three to five years in state prison but said that the brothers’ mother supported probation rather than incarceration because she felt losing another son would be devastating.
Ayres said Christopher returned home from work between 6:30 and 7 p.m., consumed eight Smirnoff vodka nips while carrying a Ruger American 9mm semiautomatic handgun holstered on his hip, and later placed it on his stomach while watching television due to discomfort. After Johnathan entered the room and handled the gun before returning it to Christopher’s stomach, Christopher later handled the gun again when it fired and struck Johnathan in the chest.
Johnathan Lacour was transported to UMass Memorial Medical Center – University Campus in Worcester, where he was pronounced dead shortly after midnight. According to court documents referenced by police statements read during proceedings, Christopher told officers he had pointed the gun at his brother “as a joke” without realizing there was a round chambered.
Monopoli said Christopher Lacour had never previously been charged with any crime and that he was legally licensed for firearm possession at the time of the incident. He described Johnathan as both an older brother and best friend to Christopher, emphasizing that both their mother and family have been deeply affected by what happened.
summary: Judge Daniel M. Wrenn accepted the plea and imposed conditions including substance abuse evaluation and treatment if necessary, as well as a prohibition on possessing firearms. Assistant District Attorney Thomas Ayres had sought a sentence of three to five years in state prison but said that the brothers’ mother supported probation rather than incarceration because she felt losing another son would be devastating.
